load_block.note: W::new takes the 64-byte block as one fixed-size array and reads its sixteen words with u32::from_be_bytes over chunks_exact(4), so the compiler drops the per-word slice bounds checks and four-byte shift-or chains that load_be(&input[offset..]) needed.

hkdf_rekey_once.note: HKDF::expand keys HMAC with the PRK once and clones the keyed state for every 32-byte output block, instead of building a new HMAC (padding the key and compressing the inner pad block) per block; the output is unchanged.
